message:
Hello Everyone,

I'm still here and am still fighting. 60 minutes sounds like a great idea. I am well documented. Presently I have my last complaint in the review stage with the Maryland PSC. This is a mess that Mike said in the beginning that its so much wrong here. I don't know if any of you have experienced this or not. It is something that is called a PVP(payment verification point). They allow you a certain amount on your phone calls and when you reach 75% you have to call them and they in turn contact Verizon to see if you have paid your phone bill. You are authorizing Verizon to share your personal information with them on the line.

I will be attending the TasteofJustice fair at the Martin Luther Library in D.C. tomorrow, it is from 10am to 5pm. I will have to update the New York Campaign for Telephone Justice as to what is going on. They have been fighting the N.Y. telephone issue for a long time but are not aware of this T-Netix,Evercom, Securus thing. This is indeed a monopoly. These two companies are everywhere.

There is something that the rest of you can do that hopefully will cause the FCC to act. I have done it. I sent the FCC a petition for rulemaking. You do not have to send in anything that is lengthy. Ask them to abolish exclusive contracts with DOC's and the phone companies and to abolish all commissions paid to the DOC's. If you have documentation to support T-NETIX and Evercom abuses please send it along.

Another thing, all these other inmate phone providers are using CBS for their billing. This company is incompetent, this is based upon written documentation that I have with my PSC. They claimed that they notified me by recording after my line was blocked. The PSC made them give a detailed record of all calls, I had a collect call on a day that they claimed the line was blocked.

Its a lot to this big mess. Will keep you all posted.
